strings.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
strings.summary: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is a Nigerian-born economist trained at Harvard and MIT who spent much of her career at the World Bank. She twice served as Nigeria’s finance minister, working on debt relief and fiscal reform. In 2021 she became the WTO’s first female and first African director-general. Her second term began in 2025 amid trade tensions and pressure for institutional reform.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable early life, education and career transitions; checked through 13 November 2026, not a complete news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Served as Nigeria’s finance minister and became the WTO’s first female and first African director-general, advancing international trade and development cooperation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: AB in economics, Harvard University; PhD in regional economics and development, MIT
strings.highlights.h1.title: Fiscal and debt reform
strings.highlights.h1.text: Twice served as Nigeria’s finance minister and helped negotiate Paris Club debt relief in 2005.
strings.highlights.h2.title: WTO leadership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Became WTO director-general in 2021, the first woman and first African in the role.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Second term began
strings.timeline.t1.text: Began a second four-year term as WTO director-general after members reappointed her in 2024.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Took charge of WTO
strings.timeline.t2.text: Took office as director-general, the first woman and first African to lead the WTO.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Second finance ministry term
strings.timeline.t3.text: Returned as Nigeria’s finance minister and coordinating minister for the economy, serving until 2015.
strings.timeline.t4.title: World Bank managing director
strings.timeline.t4.text: Returned to the World Bank as managing director, continuing senior leadership in international development.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Debt relief negotiations
strings.timeline.t5.text: As finance minister helped negotiate Paris Club debt relief, addressing Nigeria’s external debt.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First finance ministry term
strings.timeline.t6.text: Left the World Bank to become Nigeria’s finance minister, the first woman to hold the post.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctoral training
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed a PhD in regional economics and development at MIT before a career in international development.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Nigerian childhood
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Ogwashi-Uku, Nigeria, and later studied at Harvard and MIT in the United States.
